current_answer: As of 15 September 2026 at 12:00 UTC, no broad cross-model core-capability decline is proven. The new signal is sharper on usable access: OpenAI's status history records resolved Work Mode and GPT-5.6 paid-plan errors on 15 September, while a fresh Sol High report says one bounded task exhausted two five-hour windows with 10.7M cached input tokens and remained incomplete. Official guidance says model, task, context, reasoning, Fast mode, and multistep work all change allowance use. Astra still has a real mixed benchmark picture—strong gains beside a GDPval/presentation slice loss—but current evidence points to a broken or expensive assembled work system more confidently than to broad weight decline. Audit surface, context, served model, tool trace, artifact, and allowance before switching.

catalogue_card.question: Are popular AI models getting worse right now?
catalogue_card.text: No broad decline is proven—but today’s answer is worse as a work-system diagnosis: OpenAI logged fresh Work Mode/GPT-5.6 errors, and a Sol control burned two five-hour windows on one unfinished task. Check the lane before blaming the weights.

summary: No broad cross-model core-capability decline is proven, but the usable-work system has a sharper current failure signal.
OpenAI status records list resolved Work Mode errors and GPT-5.6/GPT-5.6 Instant paid-plan errors on 15 September; that is availability evidence, not a weight-change finding.
A fresh GPT-5.6 Sol High issue reports two exhausted five-hour windows on one incomplete task, with 10.7M cached input tokens and weekly allowance moving from 53% to 37%.
A separate Plus issue reports an idle weekly-meter jump and reset-date change before a limit rejection; account reconciliation is still missing.
OpenAI’s usage guide says model, task, context, output, reasoning effort, Fast mode, and multistep work change allowance use; higher effort does not always improve results.
Astra’s independent benchmark picture remains mixed: strong intelligence/coding slices alongside a GDPval-AA v2 and presentation-quality loss, with no temporal decline test.
Reader move: record surface, route, context, effort, cached input, tool trace, artifact, allowance, and provider status; replay with a control before switching.
uncertainty: Fresh status incidents establish availability failures, not a model-weight change or prevalence estimate.
The Sol quota report is one uncontrolled account report without server-ledger reconciliation or a matched Astra task.
Astra benchmark results remain cross-sectional or harness-specific; no public matched longitudinal cross-provider capability series is available.
No first-party audience analytics, representative prevalence sample, or willingness-to-pay evidence is available.
freshness_note: Fresh public-source check completed 15 September 2026. Official incidents and a non-Astra Sol control materially sharpen the usable-access diagnosis while leaving broad capability decline unproven.
